name: jiter
input_api: jiter.from_json(local JSON bytes) with documented defaults (cache_mode='all', partial_mode=False, allow_inf_nan=True, float_mode='float')
scope: JSON structure and values from local bytes; valid nested-object and nested-array controls, each equal to a hand-written tree summary and an exact type-tagged CPython json oracle tree
family: Jiter 0.19.0 Rust parser (PythonParser over jiter::parse::Parser) / lexical-parse-float 1.0.6
family_note: jiter.from_json is the standalone PyO3 module in crates/jiter-python; it calls PythonParse::python_parse in the Jiter crate's python.rs, which drives parse.rs, string_decoder.rs and number_decoder.rs and builds Python objects directly (value.rs JsonValue is not used). Floats go through lexical-parse-float. Same Jiter parser family as the selected pydantic path (pydantic-core 2.50.4 embeds Jiter 0.18.0 and parses through JsonValue), so this is not an independent parser family and its downloads are not added to Pydantic's. crates/jiter/src is byte-identical to the crates.io jiter 0.19.0 crate used by the Rust JSON cell's jiter path. The package README recommends using jiter directly only when not using pydantic.
number_and_key_scope: Not exercised beyond the controls; no malformed or edge-case probes were run. From the pinned source: duplicate object keys are inserted with PyDict_SetItem, so the last value wins unless catch_duplicate_keys=True; with the num-bigint feature, integers beyond i64 become arbitrary-precision Python ints; allow_inf_nan defaults to True, so the non-RFC NaN, Infinity and -Infinity tokens are accepted; nesting is limited to 200 levels (DEFAULT_RECURSION_LIMIT). The controls contain no duplicate keys (checked with the oracle's object_pairs_hook), only exactly representable floats (-0.25e1 and 2.5e-1) and small integers.

name: json5
input_api: json5.loads(local JSON bytes); json5.loads(decoded str) and json5.load(BytesIO(local bytes)) give the same exact tree on both controls
scope: JSON structure and values from local bytes; valid nested object and nested array controls, each equal to an exact type-tagged CPython json oracle tree. JSON5 superset parser: it accepts JSON5-only syntax and so does not reject non-RFC 8259 input.
family: json5 pure-Python PEG parser (glop-generated json5/parser.py) with AST conversion in json5/lib.py
family_note: json5.loads decodes bytes as UTF-8, runs the Parser class that glop 0.9.0 generated from the project's JSON5 grammar, then walks the AST in lib.py, calling Python int() and float() on number lexemes. It neither imports nor delegates to the standard json module. Independent of the CPython json (_json scanner), simplejson, UltraJSON, Jiter, orjson/yyjson, YAJL, msgspec, RapidJSON and simdjson families in this cell. Unrelated to the Cython pyjson5 package and to the JavaScript json5 package beyond the shared JSON5 grammar.
number_and_key_scope: Not exercised beyond the controls; no malformed or edge-case probes were run. From the pinned lib.py source: duplicate object keys are allowed by default and dict(pairs) keeps the last value (allow_duplicate_keys=False rejects them); integers go through Python int() (arbitrary precision), numbers with '.', 'e' or 'E' through float(); hexadecimal, Infinity and NaN JSON5 tokens are accepted. The controls contain no duplicate keys (checked with the oracle's object_pairs_hook), only exactly representable floats (1.25 and 2.5e-1) and small integers.

name: python-rapidjson
input_api: rapidjson.load(io.BytesIO(local JSON bytes)); rapidjson.loads(bytes) and rapidjson.loads(decoded str) give the same exact tree on both controls
scope: JSON structure and values from a local binary stream; valid nested object and nested array controls, each equal to an exact type-tagged CPython json oracle tree
family: Tencent RapidJSON C++ SAX Reader (vendored v1.1.0-763-g24b5e7a8) / python-rapidjson PyHandler wrapper
family_note: rapidjson.load wraps the stream in PyReadStreamWrapper (chunked .read() calls) and drives RapidJSON's GenericReader::Parse with python-rapidjson's own PyHandler, which builds Python objects from SAX events. This is the same Tencent RapidJSON C++ parser family as the C++ RapidJSON path (projects/json/cpp/rapidjson, release 1.1.0, which reaches the same GenericReader through Document::Parse with RapidJSON's own number conversion), at a later upstream revision; it is not an independent parser from that path. Independent of the CPython json, simplejson, Jiter, orjson/yyjson, yajl, msgspec and UltraJSON families in this cell.
number_and_key_scope: Not exercised beyond the controls; no malformed or edge-case probes were run. From the pinned rapidjson.cpp source: the default number_mode (NM_NAN) parses with kParseNumbersAsStringsFlag | kParseNanAndInfFlag, so RapidJSON's own strtod is bypassed and PyHandler::RawNumber converts integers with PyLong_FromString (arbitrary precision) and other numbers with CPython's PyOS_string_to_double; NaN, Infinity and -Infinity are accepted unless allow_nan=False. Duplicate object keys are inserted with PyDict_SetItem, so the last value wins. load() passes stream chunks to RapidJSON without kParseValidateEncodingFlag, so UTF-8 validity of bytes streams is not checked by the parser. The controls contain no duplicate keys (checked with the oracle's object_pairs_hook), only exactly representable floats (1.25 and 2.5e-1) and small integers.
